column10: MEASURED 2026-08-05 15:36 by LOCK THIS AXIS at the console. The controller accepted it: OK LIM J0 MIN=29 MAX=110 CAL=1 (FW 1.0.0 console 1.2.0). Evidence: Downloads/calibration-row-J0.csv. RESTORED 2026-08-06 after being overwritten: the 0-180 sweep earlier that day widened this row to the servo's full electrical range without checking for an existing lock - one existed and this file did not know about it. Widening min from 29 to 0 handed back 29 degrees the operator had already measured as unreachable; commanding into that region drives the joint against a mechanical stop and the servo stalls there. Do not widen this row again without a new measurement. These are ACCEPTED COMMANDED SOFT LIMITS - angles the operator drove to and chose - NOT mechanical extremes. MG996R (type INFERRED from the BOM). Support the arm against rotation while testing. MEASURED 2026-08-05 18:05 by LOCK THIS AXIS at the console. The controller accepted it: OK LIM J1 MIN=0 MAX=84 CAL=1 (FW 1.0.0 console 1.2.0). These are ACCEPTED COMMANDED SOFT LIMITS - the angles the operator drove to and chose - NOT the joint's mechanical extremes; nothing in this system can observe those. home_deg 1 is where it was settled at lock time. mirror_mode=inverted set 2026-08-05 at the operator's instruction so the two shoulder servos turn OPPOSITE ways. The firmware drives D5 to (180 + 2*mirror_offset_deg) - D4; with the offset at 0 that is 180 - D4 - so D4 at 60 puts D5 at 120. THIS IS STILL NOT A MEASUREMENT. mirror_offset_deg is 0 because nobody has measured it; 0 assumes both horns were splined perfectly symmetrically about 90 and MG996R horns step in whole teeth of about 18 degrees so that is the exception not the rule. If the real mirror axis is not 90 the pair fight each other by twice the error the whole time joint 1 is enabled - they hold; get hot; strip a gear. Measure it: linkage UNBOLTED and horns off; single-servo sketch on D4 and D5 SEPARATELY and never paired; find angles a and b that point both output shafts the same physical way; mirror_offset_deg = (a + b) / 2 - 90. THE LOCKED TRAVEL DOES NOT SETTLE THE OFFSET: 0-84 mirrors to 96-180 at offset 0 and both ends are legal - so this range would be accepted whether or not the axis is really 90. It buys clearance; it is not evidence. Any non-zero offset measured later shifts that image and may force this row to narrow. MIR is refused while joint 1 is enabled (E9) so disable it or reconnect before reloading this file. Two MG996R (type INFERRED from the BOM) - in spec on the 6.62V supply.
